title: PAYG-tier-thresholds-scratchpad
content:
Quick back-of-envelope notes for pricing tiers / unit econ — mostly for my head and to share with Dan/Ivy. Rough, lots of TODOs and questions.

Context / goals:
- Need simple starter + pro + enterprise anchors for hosted API that map to unit economics and encourage growth into Dedicated.
- Show 3 price levers: per-token PAYG, committed monthly bundles, reserved capacity commitments for enterprise.
- Keep free tier meaningful but not abusive.

ASSUMPTIONS (very rough; will refine with infra):
- GPU amortized cost (incl infra, ops, cooling, license): $2.50 / GPU-hour (conservative cheap infra region).
- Typical model profile we expect to push on hosted: 4-bit quantized 13B variant. Effective throughput: ~150 tokens/sec per GPU at steady-state for short requests (avg seq 64).
- Utilization target for hosted pool baseline: 60% (bursty demand + slack for spikes).
- Storage / network / infra overhead per token: ~20% on top of compute cost (caching, routing, SLO buffers).

BASIC MATH: compute tokens/hr per GPU = 150 tps * 3600 = 540,000 tokens/hr.
Effective tokens/hr @ 60% util = 324,000 tokens/hr.
Compute cost per effective token = $2.50 / 324,000 = $0.000007716 / token -> $0.007716 per 1k tokens.
Add 20% infra/mgmt overhead -> $0.00926 per 1k tokens (round to $0.0093).
Add margin + SG&A + support + amortized acquisition (~3x) -> target price per 1k tokens PAYG ~ $0.028-$0.035.

Sanity checks:
- If we price PAYG at $0.03 / 1k tokens, gross margin vs compute-only ~ 3.2x (0.03 / 0.0093). Reasonable to cover ops and growth.
- Embeddings: different profile – lower inference ops but more memory. Assume embeddings cost ~0.5x token compute cost per 1k tokens because batchable and shorter sequences -> base cost per 1k embedding-tokens ~$0.0045; price at $0.015 per 1k embedding-tokens.

Tier sketches (starter ideas):
- Free: 200k tokens / month + 50 embedding-requests free (small dev/test). Hard cap to prevent heavy users.
- Starter (pay monthly): $29 / month includes 3M tokens + 50k embedding units. Overage PAYG at $0.025 / 1k.
- Growth: $199 / month includes 20M tokens + 200k embedding units. Overage at $0.02 / 1k.
- Pro: $999 / month includes 150M tokens + 1M embedding units. Overage at $0.012 / 1k.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: custom, pricing anchored to reserved capacity (committed GPU-hours) with effective tokens-per-month guarantees; typical discounts 40–70% vs PAYG depending on commitment and SLA.

Rationale for numbers:
- Starter price: $29 covers fixed costs and yields low usage CAC funnel. If a starter user uses entire 3M tokens, implied unit price = $29 / 3M = $0.00967 / 1k tokens (below PAYG) -> encourages plan conversion but still above compute cost.
- Growth / Pro step-downs are compression from volume. We need to ensure pro still > compute+ops at target utilization to avoid negative margin. At 150M tokens included in Pro, implied unit price = $0.00666 / 1k tokens — that would be below earlier compute+overhead -> so Pro needs to be primarily for higher ARR customers who we expect to convert to Dedicated (or we ensure higher renewal economics via add-ons).

Committed capacity thought experiment (enterprise):
- Enterprise wants 30k rps sustained (example) -> translates to N GPUs. Need mapping of rps->tokens/sec based on avg request size.
- Offer reserved pool price: baseline $1.80 / GPU-hr (private large commitment) -> if enterprise commits 24/7 then effective tokens cost drops hugely.

Sensitivity table (quick):
- If throughput is 100 tps instead of 150: compute cost per 1k tokens -> $2.50 / (100*3600*0.6) *1000 = $0.013 = $0.013 per 1k -> after infra 20% = $0.0156 -> need PAYG ~ $0.05+ / 1k. So throughput is the single biggest driver.
- If util is 40% instead of 60%: compute cost per 1k increases proportionally.

Billing mechanics / UX notes:
- Show "included tokens" prominently; bill fractional tokens per request (not round up).
- Overage in 1k-token increments on PAYG buckets.
- Provide an "effective unit price" meter in Console so customers can see their realized $/1k aggregated (tokens consumed, cache hit rates, batching savings).

Promotion hooks / marketing angles:
- Starter bundles with predictable cost are attractive for product teams testing features (avoids surprise PAYG bills).
- Show a chart: "If you hit X monthly tokens, plan Y gives you N% savings vs PAYG."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need exact infra cost breakdown from Infra/Finance: cooling, KMS, egress, redis/KV cache, tracing retention overhead -> ask infra for a per-GPU-hour cost table by region. (@Daniel)
- Need to measure real-world throughput numbers for the three model families (7B, 13B quant, 70B q4f16) under our serving runtime for representative seq lengths. Run load tests with sample prompt mix. (@Ivy)
- Decide on embedding unit definition (1 embedding request = average 256 tokens input? or per call?). Standardize across docs.
- How to price function-calling / tools costs where backend ops (tooling webhooks executor) add additional infra? Consider add-on billing for tool-exec minutes.
- Legal/tax implications for credits / free-tier promos in EU/APAC (VAT differences) -> loop in finance.

Next steps (practical):
- Pull infra numbers and run a small notebook to generate a matrix of prices vs utilization vs throughput (sweep). Link to notebook in linked_artifacts.
- Propose initial public-facing numbers for internal review (draft PRD).
- Build Console UX mock for included tokens meter and top-of-bill alert when monthly runrate > 3x plan.

Quick notes to self:
- Keep PAYG headline simple: $0.03 / 1k tokens (text gen) and $0.015 / 1k embedding-tokens as a public anchor while we validate numbers.
- Use discounts for monthly prepay vs true PAYG usage: 10% for monthly prepays, 25–50% for 12mo commitments depending on size.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to cleaner PRD after infra + RW numbers come in.
